notes: Help page gives no model (only str). Littell et al. (2006, SAS for Mixed Models, 2nd ed.) Chapter_8.sas holds these 60 rows as Data Set 8.2 (Data Set 7.2 of the 1996 edition) and fits proc mixed, model yield = moist, random int moist / type=un sub=variety (Outputs 8.1-8.3), a random-coefficient regression with correlated variety intercepts and moisture slopes; Output 8.4 refits it with type=un(1), the covariance fixed at zero. Variety is an ordered factor but a grouping id. Outside check: stands.

formula: mathgain ~ ses + minority + poly(mathkind, 3) + ses:minority + (1 | schoolid) + (1 | classid)
notes: Help page describes the Study of Instructional Improvement (outcome mathgain) and gives no formula. Galecki and Burzykowski's chapter 18 code (nlmeU 0.71.7, inst/scriptsR4.5.1/Ch18lme.R) starts from M18.1 = lme(mathgain ~ ses + minority + mathkind + sex + housepov, random = list(schoolid = ~1, classid = ~1)), adds sex:housepov (M18.2), drops sex and housepov (M18.3), takes a cubic in mathkind (M18.4; M18.5 a B-spline instead) and ends with M18.6, which adds ses:minority; Ch18mer.R refits M18.6 as lmer(mathgain ~ ses + minority + poly(mathkind, 3) + ses:minority + (1|schoolid) + (1|classid)). West, Welch and Galecki's chapter 4 (WWGbook ch04.R) fits Models 4.1-4.4 on classroom, the table this one was built from. classid codes are unique across schools. childid is the pupil id; mathknow has missing values. Outside check: the book's final model replaces the recalled one with every covariate.

formula: visual ~ visual0 + time + treat.f + (1 + time || subject)
notes: Help page describes the ARMD trial (visual acuity at 4, 12, 24 and 52 weeks) and gives no formula. Galecki and Burzykowski's chapter 16 code (nlmeU 0.71.7, inst/scriptsR4.5.1/Ch16lme.R) starts from M16.1 = lme(visual ~ visual0 + time + treat.f + treat.f:time, random = ~1 | subject), adds a varPower(time) residual variance (M16.2), a correlated time slope (M16.3), makes it uncorrelated with pdDiag (M16.4) and ends with M16.5, which drops treat.f:time: lme(visual ~ visual0 + time + treat.f, random = list(subject = pdDiag(~time)), weights = varPower(form = ~time)). Ch16mer.R refits M16.1 and M16.7 (M16.4 without varPower) with lmer. The residual variance function is not part of the formula. time.f and tp are alternate time codings and miss.pat the missingness pattern, all ignored. Outside check: the book's final model replaces the first fit.

formula: spec.fo ~ prt.f*occ.f + sex.f*age.f + bmi + fiber.f + prt.f:fiber.f + occ.f:fiber.f + (1 + fiber.f*occ.f | id)
notes: Help page describes the Progressive Resistance Training trial (muscle fibers within subjects); prt merges prt.subjects and prt.fiber. Galecki and Burzykowski's chapter 17 code (nlmeU 0.71.7, inst/scriptsR4.5.1/Ch17part1.R) fits M17.1 on Type 1 fibers, lme(spec.fo ~ (prt.f + occ.f)^2 + sex.f + age.f + sex.f:age.f + bmi, random = ~occ.f - 1 | id), then M17.3 on both types, adding fiber.f, prt.f:fiber.f and occ.f:fiber.f with random = ~occ.f:fiber.f - 1 | id, a general 4 x 4 covariance; M17.3a refits it as random = ~1 + fiber.f + occ.f + fiber.f:occ.f | id. random_slopes lists the fiber.f and occ.f slopes, since an interaction is no slope term; the formula keeps the fiber.f:occ.f slope. iso.fo is model 2's response. Outside check: M17.3 replaces the intercept-only reading.

formula: log(iso.fo) ~ age.f + sex.f + occ.f + prt.f + (1 | id)
notes: Claflin et al. (2011, J Appl Physiol 111, Statistical analysis; PMC3191797) fit log isometric force (Fo, iso.fo here) per fiber type in PROC MIXED: Age Group + Sex + Time + Time x Training Group + a random subject intercept, the interaction dropped where not significant and the reduced model reported; Fig. 5 reports Fo's training effect adjusted for sex, age and training group, so the reduced model is filed. The fits per fiber type stay in notes. fiber.f and bmi are unused usable columns. Outside check: a model the table's rows missed.

The soup help gives no model (A-not-A discrimination with sureness; Christensen, Cleaver and Brockhoff 2011). The clmm help (ordinal 2026.7-26) fits mm1 = clmm(SURENESS ~ PROD + (1|RESP) + (1|RESP:PROD), link = "probit", threshold = "equidistant") and mm2, without RESP:PROD, as the null of its test of the random effect. RESP:PROD holds a respondent's ratings of one product type. PRODID, DAY, SOUPTYPE, SOUPFREQ, COLD, EASY, GENDER, AGEGROUP and LOCATION are unused usable covariates. Domain psychology_neuroscience for the perceptual discrimination task (reporting only; Unilever consumer research, could read as industry). Outside check: mm1 replaces its test's null.

geepack's help example fits geese fit.88 (waves 1-5: as.factor(wave) + contr + I(time/100*contr) - 1) and fit.89 (waves 6-13: as.factor(wave) + contr - 1), GEE with an AR1 working correlation and cluster id = tree (Diggle, Liang and Zeger 1994), contr = 1 - (ozone == enriched). The GEE cluster is rendered as a random intercept (geepack ruling, m3#22), and the formula joins the two fits on the whole table, the subsets in notes. The four chambers (two per ozone level) are a design factor: no documented model fits them, and four levels fail the five-level rule. MASS's Sitka and Sitka89 hold the same values. Outside check: chamber leaves the grouping, which spot check #22 had added; the GEE fits keep published_model yes.

Help fits a fixed beta regression, betareg(y ~ gen + bunt + gen:bunt) on y = pct/100 + .001, and suggests bunt should be a random effect (Salmon 1938); the 20 bunt types represent the 69 in the experiment. Rendered with bunt random, the strong gen:bunt interaction as the random term bunt:gen and the layout repeat rep fixed (spot check #22). pct is a percentage, so continuous; infected and total counts are unavailable. Outside check: the help suggests the random bunt effect but fits none, so published_model turns no.

boot help (Davison and Hinkley 1997): 14 pairs of locations, one site per pair given a warning sign, speeds of about 100 cars per site in each of three periods (before, shortly after and long after the sign's erection); the design is described, no model fitted. pair:warning is the site, observed in all three periods; period and warning are numeric codes rendered as factors, and the sign's effect is the period by warning interaction, which an inferred trial model carries (#180). Outside check: the site joins the grouping and the interaction is added; the help names speed as the measurement, so the response is not inferred.

boot help: eight NBS experiments (May 1934 to July 1935), each producing replicate estimates of g by the reversible pendulum, its configuration changed between experiments; one-way grouping by series. Cressie (1982) and Davison and Hinkley (1997) compare and weight the series means; no mixed model is stated. Outside check: stands; the help names g as each experiment's estimate, so the response is not inferred.

formula: piq ~ asymptotic recovery theta1 + theta2*exp(-theta3*days), theta1 and theta2 linear in sqrt(duration), theta3 common; correlated random theta1 and theta2 by id
notes: NONLINEAR: Fox and Weisberg's appendix on mixed models (2014, sec. 4; utstat.toronto.edu/reid/sta2101f/Appendix-Mixed-Models.pdf) fits Wong, Monette and Weiner's (2001) asymptotic recovery model, wong.mod.1 = nlme(piq ~ theta1 + theta2*exp(-theta3*days), fixed = list(theta1 ~ 1 + sqrt(duration), theta2 ~ 1 + sqrt(duration), theta3 ~ 1), random = list(id = list(theta1 ~ 1, theta2 ~ 1))), and rejects a random theta3 (wong.mod.2) by its likelihood-ratio test. 200 patients after traumatic brain injury, 331 measurements, about half of the patients measured once. sex and age are unused usable columns; viq, the verbal IQ, is an alternate response. Outside check: the nonlinear model replaces the inferred random intercept.

formula: height ~ treatment*age + (age | case) + a penalized spline in age per treatment and a penalized spline deviation in age per case, their coefficients iid random
notes: Repeated heights of 197 girls with acute lymphoblastic leukemia, 1-21 per girl (1988 rows). Durban's course notes (Splines con penalizaciones, 2016, ch. 3; Psplines.pdf pp. 37-46) fit model1 = lme(altura ~ factor(tratamiento) + edad, random = ~1 | caso), then a P-spline in age (model2), a correlated random age slope (model3), a P-spline per treatment (model4) and model5, which adds each girl's penalized spline deviation from her group's curve; a restricted likelihood-ratio test keeps the deviations. The splines stay in the formula only. The page says values were changed for confidentiality, not that they are simulated. Outside check: the final spline model replaces the first fit.

Hodges (1998, JRSS B 60) hierarchical-model example: 341 health plans for federal employees in 45 states. Rigby and Stasinopoulos's gamlss book draft (2008, ch. 14, pp. 316-324) states Hodges's model as a normal one-way random effects model of the individual premium prind with a random state intercept, then fits BCT models with random state effects in the location and scale (gamlss random(state), gamlssNP). plan is a within-state code; prfam and enfam are the family premium and enrollment alternates; enind is an unused usable column. State-level covariates (expe, region) are in hodges1, not this table. Outside check: the documented one-way model replaces the reading's enind covariate.

Smoking-cessation meta-analysis (Silagy et al. 2003): 27 studies (study = studyname x year), control and nicotine-gum arms (fac), quitters d of n. Rigby and Stasinopoulos's gamlss book draft (2008, sec. 13.2.1, pp. 299-304) fits gamlssNP(cbind(d, n - d) ~ fac, random = ~fac | study, K = 10, family = BI), a random study intercept and treatment effect with a nonparametric joint distribution of 10 mass points, after Aitkin (1999). Skrondal and Rabe-Hesketh (2004, sec. 9.5; UCLA's Mplus replication) fit normal random intercepts and treatment slopes, uncorrelated, treatment coded -0.5 and 0.5. studyname and year are the components of the study id. Outside check: the documented random treatment effect is added.

Speed-of-light measurements, five experiments (Expt) of 20 consecutive runs each. Venables and Ripley's ch01.R (MASS 7.3-66) fits aov(Speed ~ Run + Expt), drops Run (Speed ~ Expt) and compares the two; Expt is fixed there and rendered random by the fixed-block ruling. Run is the within-experiment run index (ignore). Outside check: confidence turns low, as for a fixed-effects fit over blocks.

Matched case-control study, 217 pairs (Kelsey and Hardy 1975); ID is the matched pair, two rows each. HSAUR3's logistic regression chapter (Ch_logistic_regression_glm.R) fits clogit(I(status == "case") ~ driver + suburban + strata(ID)), rendered as a random-intercept logistic on the pair (amlxray ruling, m3#23). status is a two-level factor, its recode in the formula. Outside check: the recode joins the formula; published_model stays yes, as for amlxray.

Panel Study of Income Dynamics subset, 85 people followed yearly. Faraway's ELM repmeas.R sets cyear = year - 78 and fits mmod = lmer(log(income) ~ cyear*sex + age + educ + (cyear|person)), then tests cyear:sex against mmodr; year is kept uncentered, the same model. Faraway's rexamples longitfreq.md refits it with uncorrelated intercepts and slopes for other software. Outside check: stands.

Repeated log-size measurements of 79 Sitka spruce trees (54 in ozone-enriched chambers, 25 controls), five times in 1988 (Diggle, Liang and Zeger 1994). Venables and Ripley's ch10.R (MASS 7.3-66) fits sitka.lme = lme(size ~ treat*ordered(Time), random = ~1 | tree), then sitka.lme2 with ordered(Time) + treat + treatslope, treatslope = Time * (treat == "ozone"), and keeps it; sec. 10.3 fits a nonlinear growth curve (sitka.nlme, asymptotic in Time - 100, with a CAR1 variant). geepack's spruce example fits the same structure as a GEE (fit.88). Time is categorical in the main effect and linear in the ozone slope. geepack's spruce holds the same values. Outside check: the book's final linear model replaces the linear time trend.

Repeated log-size measurements of the 79 Sitka spruce trees of Sitka, eight times in 1989 (Diggle, Liang and Zeger 1994). MASS fits no model on it (its exercise 10.5 asks for an analysis). geepack's spruce holds these values as waves 6-13, and its help example fits fit.89 = geese(logsize ~ as.factor(wave) + contr - 1, id = id, corstr = "ar1"), contr the control indicator, a GEE on tree rendered as a random intercept (geepack ruling, m3#22). Outside check: geepack's fit on the same values replaces the inferred growth curve.

Nested sampling design stated on the help page (Lentner and Bishop 1986): 3 growers selected at random, 4 boxes at random per grower, 3 clusters per box; no fitted model read. Three growers fail the five-level rule, so grower is a design factor; box (1-4) repeats across growers, so the box is the composite grower:box. cluster (1-3) is the within-box observation id, ignored. Outside check: grower leaves the grouping and published_model turns no; the help names the cluster weights, so the response is not inferred.

Balance experiment (Steele 1998): 40 subjects, each tested twice under every Surface x Vision combination; CTSIB is a four-point ordinal balance scale. Faraway's ELM glmm.R dichotomizes it to stable = CTSIB == 1, fits glmer(stable ~ Sex + Age + Height + Weight + Surface + Vision + (1|Subject), binomial), drops the subject-level covariates (modgh2 = stable ~ Surface + Vision + (1|Subject), compared by anova) and goes on with modgh2 in its diagnostics and INLA fit. The response column stays the ordinal CTSIB. Sex, Age, Height and Weight are unused usable columns. Outside check: the reduced model replaces the first fit.

Fully nested measurement-consistency design stated on the help page (Bliss 1967): 6 labs, 2 technicians per lab, 2 samples per technician (G/H, in fact identical), 2 replicate fat measurements each. Faraway's ELM random.R fits cmod = lmer(Fat ~ 1 + (1|Lab) + (1|Lab:Technician) + (1|Lab:Technician:Sample)), tests the sample component against cmodr, without it, by a parametric bootstrap and exactRLRT, and reports bootstrap intervals for cmod. Technician (one/two) and Sample (G/H) nest within Lab, so the composites Lab:Technician and Lab:Technician:Sample. Outside check: stands.

formula: seizures ~ treat + expind + treat:expind + offset(log(timeadj)) + (1 | id)
notes: Longitudinal seizure-count trial (Thall and Vail 1990): 59 patients, an 8-week baseline and four 2-week treatment periods each (id the grouping). Faraway's ELM glmm.R drops patient 49 (epilo) and fits glmer(seizures ~ offset(log(timeadj)) + expind + treat + I(expind*treat) + (1|id), poisson, nAGQ = 25); the subset stays in notes. timeadj (weeks of period) is the offset; am.R later fits a GAMM with s(age). age is an unused usable column. Outside check: stands, the excluded patient now in notes.

Chatfield, Problem Solving: A Statistician's Guide. 39 ankylosing-spondylitis patients, the left and right hip measured per person (78 rows). Flexion after treatment is the response, flexion before a baseline covariate (dietox ruling); the rotation angles rbef and raft are alternate responses, ignored. Design described, no model stated; response chosen among the angle columns. Outside check: stands against the reply's wide reading, since the before columns are baselines and the two sides group within a person.

formula: narsp ~ I(ave(ypc, msa, FUN = function(x) x[1])) + perypc + regtest + rcdum + ajwtr + time + (1 | msa)
notes: Housing prices in 36 US metropolitan statistical areas over 1986-1994 (Frees 2004); narsp is the log average sale price, time is year 1-9, the rows sorted by time within msa. Faraway's ELM (2nd ed.) chapter 11 exercise 2 fits narsp on every other column but msa (b), replaces ypc by its first-year value per MSA (d), adds a random MSA intercept (e) and tests dropping rcdum and ajwtr (g); the exercise was read through a course solution (stat.purdue.edu/~tlzhang/stat526/solution9_s18.txt). The formula writes the first-year income as an expression; covariates names ypc. Frees's exercise 3.15 runs error-components models of narsp on ypc and year, with the supply-side columns, an AR(1) error and ypc slopes. Outside check: Faraway's exercise replaces the recalled covariates.
